αἰπήν: αἰπύς — steep, sheer; fem. acc. sg. (agreeing with πόλιν ’steep city’), distinct from the fixed phrase αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος
αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον)
αἲ: αἴ (epic = εἰ) — if, would that; particle introducing a wish + opt. (αἲ γάρ ’would that’)
αἴας: Αἴας — Ajax, son of Telamon, Greek hero at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
αἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. (αἵ μοι ἕποντο ’which followed me’)
αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv.
βαθυζώνους: βαθύζωνος — deep-girdled (wearing a long, girdled robe); stock epithet of women; fem. acc. pl.
βεβαρηότες: βαρέω — weigh down, burden; perf. part. masc. nom. pl., intransitive: ’weighed down, heavy’ (οἴνῳ βεβαρηότες ’heavy with wine’)
βουλῇ: βουλή — plan, counsel, council; fem. dat. sg. (ἐνὶ βουλῇ ’in council’)
βούλετο: βούλομαι — wish, want, prefer; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented: ’he wished’
βῆμεν: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 1 pl., unaugmented (= ἔβημεν): ’we went, we embarked’
γένοιτο: γίγνομαι — become, happen, turn out; aor. opt. 3 sg. (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’)
γίγνωσκον: γιγνώσκω — perceive, recognize, come to know; impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἐγίγνωσκον): ’I perceived, I could tell’
γεραιστὸν: Γεραιστός — Geraestus, a headland at the south of Euboea; masc. acc. sg. (place to which)
γλαυκώπιδος: γλαυκῶπις — gleaming-eyed (standing epithet of Athena); fem. gen. sg.
γυναῖκας: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. acc. pl.
δίχ: δίχα (elided δίχ’) — apart, in two, at odds; adv. (δίχ’ ἐβάζομεν ’we spoke at odds’)
δίχα: δίχα — apart, in two, asunder; adv. (δίχα ... ἥνδανε βουλή, lit. ’counsel pleased split in two’, i.e. was divided)
δαΐφρονα: δαΐφρων — wise-minded, war-minded (root disputed: linked either to δαῆναι ’learn’ or δάϊς ’battle’); masc. acc. sg., epithet of Odysseus
δαήσεαι: δαῆναι (root δα-) — learn, come to know; fut. mid. 2 sg. δαήσεαι: ’you shall learn’
δεινὸν: δεινός — dread, terrible, awesome; masc. acc. sg. (δεινὸν χόλον ’dread anger’)
δεύτερον: δεύτερος — second; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’a second time’
δεῖξε: δείκνυμι — show, point out; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδειξε): ’he showed’
διέδραμον: διατρέχω — run through, run across (δια- + τρέχω); aor. 3 pl.: ’they ran through, sped over’ (ἰχθυόεντα κέλευθα διέδραμον)
διεπέρσαμεν: διαπέρθω — sack utterly, destroy utterly (δια- intensive + πέρθω ’sack’); aor. 1 pl.: ’we utterly sacked’
διομήδεος: Διομήδης — Diomedes, son of Tydeus, Greek hero at Troy; masc. gen. sg.
δολιχὸν: δολιχός — long; masc. acc. sg. (δολιχὸν πλόον ’a long voyage’)
δόλοισι: δόλος — trick, stratagem, cunning device; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
δύναμιν: δύναμις — power, might, ability; fem. acc. sg.
δῖαν: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. acc. sg. δῖαν, here extended to the sea (ἅλα δῖαν ’the heavenly brine’) rather than a hero
δῖοι: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. pl. δῖοι, here extended to the Achaeans generally (δῖοι Ἀχαιοί) rather than a single hero
εἰνάετες: εἰνάετες — for nine years; adv. (εἰνά- epic by-form of ἐννέα ’nine’ + -ετες ’years’), cf. ἑξάετες, πεντάετές in this same part
εἰσήγαγ: εἰσάγω — lead in, bring in; aor. 3 sg., elided (εἰσήγαγ’ = εἰσήγαγε): ’he led in, brought home’
εἰσορόωντα: εἰσοράω — look upon, gaze at; pres. part. masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic εἰσορῶντα): ’as I gaze’, agreeing with an implied ’me’
εὐρέα: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα ’broad backs’ (ἐπ’ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης ’over the broad back of the sea’)
θείειν: θέω — run; pres. inf., epic θείειν (= Attic θεῖν): ’to run’ (πέρι θείειν ταχύς ’exceedingly swift to run’)
θεσπεσίῃ: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, prodigious, superhuman in scale; fem. dat. sg. (ἠχῇ θεσπεσίῃ ’with a wondrous outcry’)
θεόφιν: θεός — god; dat./instr. pl., epic suffix -φι(ν) (θεόφιν = θεοῖς): ’to/by the gods’ (θεόφιν μήστωρ ἀτάλαντος ’a counselor the equal of the gods’)
καθύπερθε: καθύπερθε(ν) — above, from above; adv., + gen.: ’above’ (καθύπερθε Χίοιο ’above Chios’)
κακά: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl., substantive: ’evils, troubles’ (πάθομεν κακά ’we suffered troubles’)
κακοῖο: κακός — bad, evil; neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ) (πῆμα κακοῖο ’woe of evil, i.e. woe upon woe’, an intensifying genitive)
κακότητα: κακότης — badness, misery, trouble; fem. acc. sg.
κακὴν: κακός — bad, evil; fem. acc. sg. (ἔριν ... κακήν ’evil strife’)
καλεσσαμένω: καλέω — call, summon; aor. mid. part., dual nom.: ’the two having called’ (τὼ καλεσσαμένω ἀγορήν ’the two having called an assembly’)
κατέκταθεν: κατακτείνω — kill, slay; aor. pass. 3 pl., root aorist in -θεν, augmented (κατ’ + ἔκταθεν; unaugmented κτάθεν elsewhere in Homer): ’were slain’
καταδύντα: καταδύω — go down, set; aor. part. masc. acc. sg. (ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα ’at the sun’s going down, at sunset’)
καταθνητῶν: καταθνητός — mortal, subject to death; masc. gen. pl. (καταθνητῶν ἀνθρώπων ’of mortal men’), epic by-form of θνητός
καταφθιμένοιο: καταφθίνω — perish, die, waste away; aor. mid. part. masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου): ’having perished, dead’
κείνων: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc./fem. gen. pl.: ’of those’
κεύσω: κεύθω — hide, conceal; fut. 1 sg.: ’I will hide’
κεῖθι: κεῖθι — there; adv., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖ)
κρήτην: Κρήτη — Crete; fem. acc. sg. (place to which, εἰσήγαγε ... Κρήτην)
κρατερὸς: κρατερός — mighty, strong, powerful; masc. nom. sg.
κτήματά: κτῆμα — possession, piece of property; neut. acc. pl.
κόσμον: κόσμος — order, arrangement, due order; masc. acc. sg. (οὐ κατὰ κόσμον ’not in due order’)
λέσβῳ: Λέσβος — Lesbos, an Aegean island; fem. dat. sg. (place where, ἐν Λέσβῳ)
ληίδ: ληΐς — booty, plunder, spoil; fem. acc. sg., elided (ληίδ’ = ληίδα) (κατὰ ληίδα ’after plunder’)
λιγὺς: λιγύς — clear-sounding, shrill, whistling; masc. nom. sg., usually of voices/instruments but here of wind (λιγὺς οὖρος ’a clear, keen wind’)
λιπέσθαι: λείπω — leave; aor. mid. inf. λιπέσθαι: ’to be left behind’ (παῖδα λιπέσθαι ’that a son be left behind’)
μάψ: μάψ — rashly, in vain, without due cause; adv.
μήδετο: μήδομαι — devise, plan, contrive; impf. 3 sg.: ’was devising, planned’
μήνιος: μῆνις — wrath, anger (esp. a god’s lasting anger); fem. gen. sg.
μήστωρ: μήστωρ — counselor, adviser, one who devises; masc. nom. sg. (θεόφιν μήστωρ ἀτάλαντος ’a counselor the equal of the gods’)
μίμαντα: Μίμας — Mimas, a windy headland on the Asia Minor coast opposite Chios; masc. acc. sg.
μαρνάμεθ: μάρναμαι — fight, do battle; 1 pl., pres.-stem form with past (impf.) force, elided (μαρνάμεθ’): ’we fought’
μαχητής: μαχητής — fighter, warrior; masc. nom. sg.
μεγαθύμου: μεγάθυμος — great-hearted, high-spirited; masc. gen. sg.
μεγακήτεα: μεγακήτης — vast, teeming with great creatures (μέγας + κῆτος ’sea-monster’); masc. acc. sg.
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μετρήσαντες: μετρέω — measure; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having measured’, of crossing a sea as if pacing it out (πέλαγος μετρήσαντες)
μηχανόωνται: μηχανάομαι — contrive, devise, scheme; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted -όωνται (= Attic -ῶνται): ’they contrive’
μιμνήσκεσθαι: μιμνήσκω — remind; mid. remember, think of; pres. inf. + gen.: ’to take thought of’ (νόστου μιμνήσκεσθαι ’to think of their return’)
μυθήσαιτο: μυθέομαι — speak, tell, relate; aor. opt. 3 sg. mid.: ’could tell’ (τίς κεν ... μυθήσαιτο ’who could tell’)
μυθείσθην: μυθέομαι — speak, tell, declare; impf. 3 dual: ’the two told’ (μῦθον μυθείσθην ’they told the matter’)
μυρμιδόνας: Μυρμιδόνες — the Myrmidons, Achilles’ own troops from Phthia; masc. acc. pl.
μῆρ: μηρός (pl. μῆρα) — thigh; sacrificial thigh-piece wrapped in fat and burned to a god; neut. acc. pl., elided (μῆρ’ = μῆρα)
μῦθοί: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; masc. nom. pl.
νέας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νέας (= Attic ναῦς)
νήεσσι: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νήεσσι (= Attic ναυσί)
νεοίμεθα: νέομαι — go, return, come; pres. opt. 1 pl., in an indirect deliberative question: ’whether we should go’
νόσφιν: νόσφιν — apart, far off, away; adv.
νόῳ: νόος — mind, thought; masc. dat. sg., instrumental: ’in mind, in thought’
νύκτα: νύξ — night; fem. acc. sg., accusative of duration: ’(through) the night’
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
νῶι: ἐγώ (dual νῶι) — we two; acc. dual: ’the two of us’ (μετὰ νῶι ’after the two of us’)
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’
ξανθὸς: ξανθός — fair-haired, yellow, tawny; masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Menelaus
οἴνῳ: οἶνος — wine; masc. dat. sg., instrumental: ’with wine’ (οἴνῳ βεβαρηότες ’heavy with wine’)
οἴσουσι: φέρω (fut. stem οἰσ-) — carry, bear; fut. 3 pl.: ’they will carry’ (οἴσουσι κλέος ’they will carry fame’)
οἶδα: οἶδα — know; perf. with pres. sense, 1 sg.: ’I know’
οὖρος: οὖρος — a fair wind, favorable wind; masc. nom. sg.
πάθομεν: πάσχω — suffer, experience; aor. 1 pl., unaugmented (= ἐπάθομεν): ’we suffered’
πάθον: πάσχω — suffer, experience; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἔπαθον): ’they suffered’
πάτροκλος: Πάτροκλος — Patroclus, companion of Achilles, killed by Hector; masc. nom. sg.
πέλαγος: πέλαγος — the open sea, high sea; neut. acc. sg.
παιπαλοέσσης: παιπαλόεις — rugged, craggy; fem. gen. sg. παιπαλοέσσης, agreeing with Χίοιο (the island-name Chios treated as feminine)
παντοίοισι: παντοῖος — of every kind, all manner of; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
παραμίμνων: παραμίμνω — remain beside, stay on; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’remaining’
παῖδα: παῖς — child, son, daughter; masc./fem. acc. sg.
πείσεσθαι: πείθω — persuade; mid./pass. fut. inf. πείσεσθαι: ’to be persuaded, to be won over’ (οὐ πείσεσθαι ἔμελλεν ’he was not to win her over’)
πεντάετές: πεντάετες — for five years; adv., cf. ἑξάετες, εἰνάετες in this same part
περιθεῖεν: περιτίθημι — place around, bestow, confer; aor. opt. 3 pl.: ’might bestow’ (δύναμιν περιθεῖεν ’might grant such power’)
πεύθομαι: πεύθομαι — learn by inquiry, hear tell, get news of; pres. 1 sg. mid., epic (= Attic πυνθάνομαι)
πλαζόμενοι: πλάζω — drive astray; mid./pass. wander, roam; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’roaming’
πλόον: πλόος — voyage, sailing, course; masc. acc. sg., epic πλόον (= Attic πλοῦν)
ποιάντιον: Ποιάντιος — son of Poias (patronymic adj., of Philoctetes); masc. acc. sg.
ποικιλομήτην: ποικιλομήτης — of shifting, many-colored cunning (ποικίλος + μῆτις); masc. acc. sg., epithet of Odysseus
ποιμένι: ποιμήν — shepherd; masc. dat. sg., in the standing royal title ποιμὴν λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’
πολέες: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl., epic πολέες (= Attic πολλοί)
πολέμου: πόλεμος — war, battle; masc. gen. sg.
πριάμοιο: Πρίαμος — Priam, king of Troy; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
προέηκεν: προΐημι — send forth, let go; aor. 3 sg., epic προέηκεν (= Attic προῆκε): ’he sent forth’ (of the wind, θεὸς προέηκεν ἀῆναι)
πυθέσθαι: πυνθάνομαι — inquire, learn, hear of; aor. inf. mid. πυθέσθαι, epexegetic: ’to hear of’ (κλέος ... πυθέσθαι ’fame ... to hear of’)
πόντος: πόντος — sea, open sea; masc. nom. sg.
σέβας: σέβας — awe, reverent wonder; neut. nom. sg. (σέβας μ’ ἔχει ’awe holds me’)
σφεων: σφεῖς — they; epic gen. pl. pron. σφέων/σφεων: ’of them’
σχέτλιος: σχέτλιος — cruel, merciless, hard-hearted; masc. nom. sg. (applied here to Zeus, an unusually harsh judgment of a god)
τέμνειν: τέμνω — cut; pres. inf., used of a sea-crossing: ’to cut across’ (πέλαγος τέμνειν ’to cut across the open sea’)
τένεδον: Τένεδος — Tenedos, a small island off the Troad; fem. acc. sg. (place to which, ἐς Τένεδον)
τέρας: τέρας — sign, portent, marvel; neut. acc. sg.
τίσασθαι: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, punish; aor. inf. mid. τίσασθαι: ’to take vengeance on’, same root as ἐτίσατο in this part
ταχὺς: ταχύς — quick, swift; masc. nom. sg. (θείειν ταχύς ’swift to run’)
τετλάμεν: τλῆναι (perf. stem τετλα-) — endure, bear, have the heart to; perf. inf. τετλάμεν, epic (= Attic τετληκέναι): ’to endure’
τεός: τεός — your, yours (2nd person possessive adj., epic = σός); masc. nom. sg.
τοιοῦτον: τοιοῦτος — such, of this kind; masc. acc. sg.
τοσσήνδε: τοσόσδε — so great, so much; fem. acc. sg., epic τοσσήνδε (double σ)
τρέπεται: τρέπω — turn; pass. be turned, changed; pres. 3 sg.: ’is changed’ (νόος τρέπεται ’the mind is changed’)
τυδέος: Τυδεύς — Tydeus, father of Diomedes; masc. gen. sg. (Τυδέος υἱός ’son of Tydeus’, periphrasis for Diomedes)
τυδεΐδεω: Τυδεΐδης — son of Tydeus (patronymic of Diomedes); masc. gen. sg., epic -εω (= Attic -ου)
φάσ: φημί — say, assert; pres. 3 pl., elided (φάσ’ = φασί): ’they say’
φαίδιμος: φαίδιμος — shining, glorious, illustrious; masc. nom. sg.
φαίης: φημί — say, assert; pres. opt. 2 sg., potential with κε: ’you would say’
φεῦγε: φεύγω — flee, escape; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφευγε): ’he fled’
φεῦγον: φεύγω — flee, escape; impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφευγον): ’I fled’
φιλοκτήτην: Φιλοκτήτης — Philoctetes, son of Poias, archer left on Lemnos and later brought to Troy; masc. acc. sg.
φραζόμεθ: φράζομαι — consider, devise, plan; impf. 1 pl. mid., elided (φραζόμεθ’ = φραζόμεθα): ’we devised’
φύγοιμεν: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. opt. 1 pl., in a purpose clause: ’that we might escape’
φῆναι: φαίνω — show, reveal, bring to light; aor. inf. φῆναι: ’to show’
χίοιο: Χίος — Chios, an Aegean island; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
χαλεπὰ: χαλεπός — harsh, difficult, severe; neut. acc. pl., substantive: ’harsh things’ (χαλεπὰ ... ὁρμαίνοντες ’pondering harsh thoughts’)
ψυρίης: Ψυρίη — Psyria, a small island near Chios; fem. gen. sg.
ἀέσαμεν: ἀέσαι (root ἀϝεσ-, distinct from ἄημι ’blow’) — pass the night; aor. 1 pl.: ’we passed the night’
ἀήμεναι: ἄημι — blow (of wind); pres. inf., epic ἀήμεναι (= Attic ἀῆναι): ’to blow’
ἀγαμέμνονι: Ἀγαμέμνων — Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, leader of the Achaeans at Troy; masc. dat. sg.
ἀθηναίης: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. gen. sg., Ionic-epic form (= Attic Ἀθηνᾶς)
ἀκούετε: ἀκούω — hear; pres. 2 pl., used with perfect force: ’you have heard’
ἀλεγεινῆς: ἀλεγεινός — painful, grievous; fem. gen. sg.
ἀλλήλοις: ἀλλήλων — one another, each other; reciprocal pron., masc. dat. pl.: ’against one another’
ἀμειβομένω: ἀμείβω — exchange; mid. answer, reply; pres. part. dual nom.: ’the two exchanging words, answering one another’
ἀμφιέποντες: ἀμφιέπω — be busy about, attend to, ply; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’busying ourselves (with)’
ἀμφιελίσσας: ἀμφιέλισσα — curved at both ends (standing epithet of ships); fem. acc. pl.
ἀμφοτέροισιν: ἀμφότερος — both; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀνέτλημεν: ἀνατλῆναι (root τλα-) — endure, bear up under; aor. 1 pl.: ’we endured’
ἀναβάντες: ἀναβαίνω — go up, go aboard, embark; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having embarked’
ἀντίλοχος: Ἀντίλοχος — Antilochus, son of Nestor, killed at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἀνόρουσαν: ἀνορούω — spring up, leap up; aor. 3 pl.: ’they sprang up’
ἀολλέσιν: ἀολλής — gathered, all together, in a body; fem. dat. pl., epic -εσιν (= Attic -εσι)
ἀπευθής: ἀπευθής — without tidings, uninformed, ignorant of news; masc. nom. sg.
ἀπηύρα: ἀπαυράω — take away, rob, deprive of; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, with an impf.-looking ending: ’took away’
ἀποστρέψαντες: ἀποστρέφω — turn back, turn away; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having turned back’
ἀπόλοντο: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy; mid. ἀπόλλυμαι, perish, be lost, die; aor. 3 pl.: ’perished’
ἀρήιος: ἀρήιος — warlike, of Ares; masc. nom. sg.
ἀργείοις: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Achaeans/Greeks; masc. dat. pl.
ἀργείοισιν: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Achaeans/Greeks; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀριστέρ: ἀριστερός — left, on the left; neut. acc. sg., elided (ἀριστέρ’ = ἀριστερά), used adverbially: ’on the left’
ἀτάλαντος: ἀτάλαντος — equal (in weight), a match for; masc. nom. sg., + dat.: ’equal to’ (θεόφιν ... ἀτάλαντος ’equal to the gods’)
ἀτάσθαλα: ἀτάσθαλος — wanton, reckless; neut. acc. pl., substantive: ’wanton, reckless deeds’, the adjective behind the fixed noun ἀτασθαλίαι ’wanton-follies’
ἀτρεΐδην: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic, here of Agamemnon); masc. acc. sg.
ἀτρεΐδῃ: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic, of Agamemnon); masc. dat. sg.
ἀτρεΐδῃσι: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic); masc. dat. pl. -ῃσι, of both sons of Atreus together, Agamemnon and Menelaus
ἀχαιοὶ: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχιλλεύς: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles, son of Peleus, chief Greek hero at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἀχιλλῆος: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles, son of Peleus, chief Greek hero at Troy; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
ἀῆναι: ἄημι — blow (of wind); aor. inf. ἀῆναι: ’to blow’ (contrast the pres. inf. ἀήμεναι elsewhere in this part)
ἄγ: ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (ἄγ’ = ἄγε): ’he led’
ἄγειραν: ἀγείρω — gather, assemble, muster; aor. 3 pl.: ’they gathered’
ἄνακτα: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. acc. sg.
ἄνακτος: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. gen. sg.
ἄργεϊ: Ἄργος — Argos; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted -εϊ (= Attic -ει)
ἄριστα: ἀγαθός (superl. ἄριστος) — best; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’best’ (ὄχ’ ἄριστα ’far the best’)
ἄρξειεν: ἄρχω — lead, begin, rule; aor. opt. 3 sg., of a repeated/general past action: ’might lead, happened to lead’
ἄσχετοι: ἄσχετος — unrestrainable, unrestrained (ἀ- + σχετός, from ἔχω); masc. nom. pl. (μένος ἄσχετοι ’unrestrained in fury’)
ἐίσας: ἐΐσος — well-balanced, even (sense disputed, perhaps ’equal on both sides’); fem. acc. pl. ἐίσας, agreeing with νῆας
ἐβάζομεν: βάζω — speak, say; impf. 1 pl.: ’we spoke’ (δίχ’ ἐβάζομεν ’we spoke at odds, disagreed’)
ἐγχεσιμώρους: ἐγχεσίμωρος — spear-wielding, spear-fierce (second element disputed: linked to μῶρος ’eager, mad’ or to μέμονα ’be eager’); masc. acc. pl., stock epithet of the Myrmidons
ἐκεῖνα: ἐκεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., neut. acc. pl.: ’those things’
ἐλαύνομεν: ἐλαύνω — drive, row, march; pres.-stem form with past narrative force, 1 pl.: ’we rowed on’
ἐλθέμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. inf., epic ἐλθέμεν (= Attic ἐλθεῖν): ’to come’
ἐλθόντες: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having come’
ἐμήσατο: μήδομαι — devise, plan, contrive; aor. 3 sg.: ’contrived’
ἐμῷ: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. dat. sg.
ἐνίκα: νικάω — conquer, surpass, excel; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἐ- + νίκα; unaugmented would be νίκα): ’surpassed’ (πολλὸν ἐνίκα ’surpassed by far’)
ἐννύχιαι: ἐννύχιος — by night, nocturnal; fem. nom. pl., used adverbially: ’by night’
ἐντιθέμεσθα: ἐντίθημι — put in, place in; mid. put aboard for oneself; impf. 1 pl. mid.: ’we loaded aboard’
ἐξακέσαιτο: ἐξακέομαι — heal completely, appease, cure; aor. opt. 3 sg. mid., in a purpose clause: ’so that he might appease’
ἐξερέοις: ἐξερέω — inquire closely, ask out, question thoroughly; opt. 2 sg., future-toned: ’you should ask about’
ἐοικότα: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting; perf. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’fitting’ (ἐοικότα μυθήσασθαι ’to speak fittingly’)
ἐοικότες: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting, resemble; perf. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’fitting’ (μῦθοι ἐοικότες ’fitting words’)
ἐπέκλωσαν: ἐπικλώθω — spin, allot by spinning (of Fate/the gods); aor. 3 pl.: ’spun out, allotted’
ἐπέσπον: ἐφέπω — follow upon, pursue, meet with; aor. 3 pl. ἐπέσπον: ’met with, incurred’ (κακὸν οἶτον ἐπέσπον ’met an evil doom’)
ἐπίφρονι: ἐπίφρων — sound of mind, prudent, sensible; fem. dat. sg.
ἐπισμυγερῶς: ἐπισμυγερῶς — most grievously, to one’s sorrow (ἐπι- intensive + σμυγερός ’woeful’); adv.
ἐρέξαμεν: ῥέζω — do, perform, esp. offer sacrifice; aor. 1 pl.: ’we offered’ (ἐρέξαμεν ἱρά ’we offered sacrifices’)
ἐρητύοντο: ἐρητύω — hold back, check, restrain; pass. be held back; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’were held back’
ἐρυκακέειν: ἐρύκω — hold back, restrain, detain; aor. inf., reduplicated epic -κακέειν (= Attic ἐρῦξαι): ’to hold back’
ἐσάωθεν: σῴζω — save, keep safe; aor. pass. 3 pl., epic ἐσάωθεν (= Attic ἐσώθησαν): ’were saved’
ἐσσομένοισι: εἰμί — be; fut. part. masc. dat. pl., epic ἐσσομένοισι (= Attic ἐσομένοις): ’to those who are to be, future generations’
ἐστόρεσεν: στόρνυμι — spread, spread smooth; aor. 3 sg.: ’spread smooth, calmed’ (of the sea)
ἐτέλεσσε: τελέω — complete, accomplish, bring to pass; aor. 3 sg., epic -εσσε (= Attic ἐτέλεσε)
ἐτίσατο: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, take vengeance on; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’took vengeance (on)’
ἐτεόν: ἐτεός — true, real; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’truly, really’ (εἰ ἐτεόν γε ’if indeed truly’)
ἐόντων: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. gen. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντων): ’of (those) being’ (θεῶν αἰὲν ἐόντων ’of the gods who are forever’)
ἐύβοιαν: Εὔβοια — Euboea, the large island off the coast of Boeotia; fem. acc. sg., printed without diaeresis (Ἐύβοιαν)
ἑήνδανε: ἁνδάνω — please, be pleasing to; impf. 3 sg., augmented ἑ- from the root’s original digamma (cf. the also-augmented, contracted ἥνδανε elsewhere in this part; unaugmented ἄνδανε); + dat.: ’was pleasing to’
ἑκατόμβας: ἑκατόμβη — hecatomb, a great sacrifice (orig. of a hundred oxen); fem. acc. pl.
ἑξάετες: ἑξάετες — for six years; adv., cf. πεντάετές, εἰνάετες in this same part
ἔθεμεν: τίθημι — put, place, lay; aor. 1 pl., augmented (the aorist stem θε- is consonant-initial, so the ἐ- shown is the augment; unaugmented θέμεν): ’we laid’ (μῆρα ἔθεμεν ’we laid the thigh-pieces on the altar’)
ἔθηκε: τίθημι — put, place, cause, bring about; aor. 3 sg., augmented (root θη-/θε-, consonant-initial; unaugmented θῆκε): ’set, caused’ (ἔριν ἔθηκε ’set strife’)
ἔκγονός: ἔκγονος — offspring, descendant; masc. nom. sg.
ἔκιχεν: κιχάνω — come upon, overtake, reach; aor. 3 sg., augmented (root κιχ-, consonant-initial; unaugmented κίχεν); the -ν is the movable ν, unrelated to the augment: ’he overtook’
ἔμελλεν: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to; impf. 3 sg., augmented (root μελλ-, consonant-initial; unaugmented μέλλε(ν)): ’was going to, was destined’
ἔμνησας: μιμνήσκω — remind; aor. 2 sg., + gen. of the thing: ’you reminded (me) of’ (ἔμνησας ὀιζύος ’you reminded me of the woe’)
ἔπλεον: πλέω — sail; impf. 3 pl.: ’they were sailing, they sailed’
ἔριν: ἔρις — strife, quarrel, contention; fem. acc. sg.
ἔσβη: σβέννυμι — quench, extinguish; pass./intr. aor. 3 sg. ἔσβη, root aorist: ’died out, was quenched’ (of the wind, not fire)
ἔχοντε: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. dual: ’the two having’ (ἕνα θυμὸν ἔχοντε ’the two of them sharing one mind’)
ἕλκομεν: ἕλκω — draw, drag, haul; pres.-stem form with past narrative force, 1 pl.: ’we drew’ (νέας ἕλκομεν ’we drew our ships down’)
ἕνα: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; masc. acc. sg. (ἕνα θυμόν ’one mind’)
ἕταροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl., epic by-form ἕταροι (= ἑταῖροι)
ἠέλιον: ἥλιος — sun; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted ἠέλιον (= Attic ἥλιον)
ἠνεμόεντα: ἠνεμόεις — windy, wind-swept; masc. acc. sg.
ἠνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἠνώγει, beside unaugmented ἀνώγει elsewhere in this part), + inf.: ’was bidding’
ἠχῇ: ἠχή — sound, outcry, din; fem. dat. sg.
ἡμίσεες: ἥμισυς — half; masc. nom. pl., epic ἡμίσεες, substantive: ’half (of them)’
ἡμετέροισι: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἤθελ: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; impf. 3 sg., elided (ἤθελ’ = ἤθελε): ’he wished’
ἤρτυε: ἀρτύω — fit together, prepare, contrive; impf. 3 sg.: ’was preparing’ (ἐπὶ ... ἤρτυε, tmesis, ’was preparing upon (us)’)
ἥνδανε: ἁνδάνω — please, be pleasing to; impf. 3 sg., augmented (η- from the root’s original digamma, contracted; the same augment as the uncontracted ἑήνδανε in this part; unaugmented ἄνδανε); + dat.: ’was pleasing to’
ἦλθ: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἦλθ’ = ἦλθε): ’he came, he returned’
ἦρα: ἦρα — favor, service (only in the idiom ἦρα φέρειν ’bring favor, curry favor’); neut./fem. acc. sg.
ἧος: ἧος — as long as, while; temporal conj., epic (= Attic ἕως)
ἰδομενεὺς: Ἰδομενεύς — Idomeneus, king of Crete, leader of the Cretan contingent at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἰχθυόεντα: ἰχθυόεις — fish-filled, teeming with fish; neut. acc. pl. (ἰχθυόεντα κέλευθα ’fish-filled paths’, of the sea)
ἱέμενοι: ἵεμαι — long for, strain toward, be eager; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’longing’ (οἴκαδε ἱέμενοι ’longing for home’)
ἱερὰς: ἱερός — sacred, holy; fem. acc. pl.
ἵκοιο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. opt. 2 sg.: ’you would arrive at’
ἵστασαν: ἵστημι — set, station; here transitive, moor (a ship); impf. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’were mooring’
ὀβριμοπάτρης: ὀβριμοπάτρη — she of the mighty father (ὄβριμος + πατήρ); fem. gen. sg., epithet of Athena
ὀιζύος: ὀιζύς — woe, misery, hardship; fem. gen. sg., governed by ἔμνησας ’you reminded (me) of’
ὀλοῆς: ὀλοός — deadly, destructive, baneful; fem. gen. sg.
ὁμοιωθήμεναι: ὁμοιόω — make like, make equal; aor. pass. inf., epic -ήμεναι (= Attic ὁμοιωθῆναι): ’to be made equal’ (μῆτιν ὁμοιωθήμεναι ’to be matched in cunning’)
ὁρμαίνοντας: ὁρμαίνω — ponder, turn over in the mind, debate; pres. part. masc. acc. pl.: ’pondering’
ὁρμαίνοντες: ὁρμαίνω — ponder, turn over in the mind, debate; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’pondering’
ὄλβον: ὄλβος — prosperity, good fortune, happiness; masc. acc. sg.
ὄχ: ὄχα — by far, exceedingly; adv., elided (ὄχ’ = ὄχα), intensifying a superlative (ὄχ’ ἄριστα ’far the best’)
ὅπῃ: ὅπῃ — where, wherever, in whatever way; relative adv.
ὅσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl.: ’all that, as much as’
ὑπένερθε: ὑπένερθε(ν) — below, underneath, beneath; adv., + gen.: ’below’ (ὑπένερθε Χίοιο ’below Chios’)
ὑπερβασίης: ὑπερβασίη — transgression, outrage, overstepping of bounds; fem. gen. sg., genitive of the charge with τίνομαι: ’for their transgression’
ὑπὲκ: ὑπέκ — out from under, forth from beneath; prep. + acc.; here in tmesis with φύγοιμεν: ’flee out from under’ (ὑπὲκ κακότητα φύγοιμεν)
ὦρσε: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse, set in motion; aor. 3 sg.: ’stirred up, roused’
ὦρτο: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse; mid./intr. aor. 3 sg. ὦρτο, root aorist: ’arose’ (of a wind springing up)
ᾐτέομεν: αἰτέω — ask, request; impf. 1 pl., augmented (αι- → ᾐ-), uncontracted ending -εομεν (= Attic ᾐτοῦμεν): ’we asked’
ῥάπτομεν: ῥάπτω — stitch, sew; fig. weave, contrive (evils); pres.-stem form with past narrative force, 1 pl.: ’we wove, we contrived’ (κακὰ ῥάπτομεν)
ῥέξαι: ῥέζω — do, perform, esp. offer sacrifice; aor. inf.: ’to offer’ (ῥέξαι ἑκατόμβας ’to offer hecatombs’)

__broaden__.ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’)
__broaden__.ὅτ: ὅτε (elided ὅτ’) — when; temporal conj., here + ἄν and subj. in a general/future clause · also + indic., of a single definite past event: ’when’ (ὅτ’ ἐν Ἄργεϊ ... ἵστασαν ’when they were mooring in Argos’)
__broaden__.θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’)
__broaden__.ἔπι: ἐπί — on, upon, over; prep. + dat., placed after its noun with anastrophe: ἑοῖς ἔπι ’upon his own (possessions)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of direction: ’toward’ (νήσου ἔπι Ψυρίης ’toward the island of Psyria’) · also as adverb with no case expressed, intensifying repetition: ’besides, again’ (ἔπι δεύτερον αὖτις ’a second time, once more’)
__broaden__.κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
__broaden__.μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’)
__broaden__.περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’)
__broaden__.παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, among; + dat. · also + gen., ’from, from the side of’ (παρ’ Ἴλου ’from Ilus’) · also + acc., of motion, ’past, along, beside’ (παρ’ Μίμαντα ’past Mimas’)
__broaden__.ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’)
__broaden__.ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic. · also + opt., in secondary sequence after a past-tense verb, indirect deliberative: ’how it might’ (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’)
__broaden__.πρίν: πρίν — before, until; conj./adv., + inf. (like Attic πρίν) · also + a temporal clause (πρίν γ’ ὅτ’ ἄν + subj.): ’until the time when’ · also πρίν κε + opt., an independent potential clause answering a suppressed protasis: ’sooner, before then’ (πρίν κεν ... ἵκοιο ’you would arrive home before then’)
